Last week at the grocery store I bought three different kinds of fish that were "previously frozen" and tossed them in my freezer. This type of fish is typically half off or close to it. I honestly don't notice a difference between taste and moistness when I go to back the fish, so I don't mind refreezing it again. Also, I realize my palette is probably shit, so whatever.

This week each day, except for yesterday, I decided to try out the different fish to see what I really liked. I prepped them all the same way. Unthawed, seasoned with salt and pepper, baked.

The fish I did this with was: * Cod * Flounder * Tilapia

I have to say, Tilapia is by far the best tasting out of the three.

Typically when I buy fish, it's salmon. I can't really tell a huge difference between fresh and farm raised taste wise, and farm raised is significantly cheaper. I think, however, is that I will stick with tilapia. The price is about right and I like the flavor almost as much as salmon.

So, anyone have any simple and good Tilapia recipes? What dishes go best with it? What are other ways I could have prepared the other fish to really bring out their flavors?

There are a few ways i like to do fish but the three main stays are. Rolled in seasoned flour and pan fried in butter. Fish tacos, roll the fish in homemade taco seasoning and pan fried. Lastly sealed in a baking paper parcel with slices of lemon, grated ginger, crushed garlic, salt and pepper, and chopped fresh chillis or dried chilli flakes. You can also substitue limes for lemons, add some sliced onion or try some different recipes you can find online. Baking the fish in a parcel keeps all the moisture in and guarantees moist cooking but i do love a good fish taco.
A lot of people say tilapia is a shit fish, but I like it. In fact, it's one of my favorite. Behind rainbow trout, of course.
Try different kinds of sauce on your fish to bring out the flavor. Lemon beurre blanc is a good start.
